newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybean futures end higher as wheat rallies.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybean futures end higher as wheat rallies.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended higher on Wednesday, supported by a late rally in wheat with light fund buying noted, traders said.
"It closed strong on the wheat gains," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
December wheat futures closed 9-1/4 cents per bushel higher at $4.00-3/4, the first close above $4 in three weeks.

Soybeans had traded on both sides of the market in choppy dealings much of the day. Volume was said to be light following Tuesday's active session with most of the moves attributed to profit taking and positioning, traders said.
Commercial buying continued to support the market with ADM Investor Services and Cargill Inc said to be buyers. Produce Grain also reportedly bought one million bushels January.
R.J. O'Brien, O'Connor and Co and Prudential Securities each bought one million January on the day, traders said.
On the sell side, Merrill Lynch Futures reportedly sold three million January and 3.5 million March on the day. Refco Inc sold 2.5 million January, traders said.
Soybeans closed seven to four cents per bushel higher with November up 4-1/4 at $6.92-3/4 a bushel and January up 4-1/4 at $6.90-1/2.
Support in the January contract was pegged at $6.69 per bushel with resistance at $6.96.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 80,000 contracts, compared with 92,631 contracts traded on Tuesday.
